_naming_rationale: The scheme-dispatch rename is not cosmetic. MiniMaxM2DecoderLayer.__init__ hard-codes prefix=f'{prefix}.mlp' when constructing the MoE submodule even though the HF attribute is `block_sparse_moe`, and vLLM's MoE weight loader translates w1/w2/w3 -> gate_proj/down_proj/up_proj via ckpt_*_proj_name kwargs at load time -- but scheme lookup runs FIRST and never sees those kwargs, so config_groups must already be in the mlp.*_proj form. The trailing bare `block_sparse_moe` -> `mlp` rule is the defensive tail for non-expert submodules (routing gates) that vLLM also places under mlp.*.
_packed_experts_rationale: MiniMax's expert weights are per-expert 2D w1/w2/w3 on disk; the packed param names here are the UNFUSED vLLM leafs the exporter emits, which is why gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj appear as `param_names` rather than the usual gate_up_proj/down_proj pair. The single format_group is the vLLM FusedMoE coupling constraint: all three projections of one expert bank must carry one scheme. `projection_splits` declares the gate_up/down ROLE buckets (which projections would share a stacked tensor on a lane that keys expert schemes per projection) -- the same declaration lfm2_moe makes for w1/w3/w2; it is what `packed_expert_role_group` reads and it reproduces the legacy fallback answer exactly.
_staging_rationale: transformers 5.x rewrites native-FP8 modules before load; for MiniMax's ModuleList-of-256-experts it swaps in FP8Experts and then tries to set experts.0.w1, which that container does not support. PrismaQuant's streaming loader reads the source FP8 bytes and applies each 128x128 weight_scale_inv block itself in _read_layer_to_device, so it never needs the rewrite.
